rules.note: The locked layer of this deployment policy: a click whose label offers a purchase is refused outright, whatever any overlay says. Jev's classifier gives button clicks NETWORK_WRITE whatever they commit, so the spend shape is recognised by the label the user would see. mergePolicyDocs carries this rule verbatim and drops overlay rules reusing its id — the M2 scenario proves that with a hostile overlay.

A submit-capable click asks a human first. The !approved clause is the gateway-level approval path: a host that carries approvals can re-present the same action with approved=true and this rule steps aside (see allow-carried-approvals). Jev's loop carries no approvals — there, an ask stops the run and the approval resumes as a new run under an amended policy, exactly as Jev's GOVERNOR_NOTES.md describes.
Standing approval, bounded by the expression itself: form fills on the local fixture host are pre-approved. The same fill on any other host falls through to the fail-closed default.
Navigation, reads, scrolls, and waits flow without asking — Jev's classifier maps exactly the provably read-only shapes to READ.
Anything a human has already approved at the gateway level may proceed. Inert inside Jev's loop (approved is always false there); it is where a carried approval lands for hosts that collect one.
